newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity prices mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity prices mostly lower.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Midwest were mostly lower Thursday as traders looked for some warmer temperatures over the next several days, brokers and markters said.
Some moderation was expected in the cool weather, which was forecast to reach as high as the high 20s degrees Fahrenheit today.

In Minnesota, Northern States Power's 544 megawatt (MW) Monticello nuclear power plant was expected to resume full power production today after tripping off line early Tuesday due to an operator error, the company said.
Separately, Union Electric's 1,125 megawatt Callaway nuclear power plant in Fulton, Mo. was also ramping up towards full power in several days following a scheduled refueling outage.
Traders also said a large generation unit would be off line through the weekend in Kansas, although the outage could not be confirmed.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were talked steady at $30.00-33.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were notionally assessed steady in the $8.50-10.00 area.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm next-day prices eased to $27.00-31.00 from $29.00-34.00 on Wednesday, the traders said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday delivery were reported to have eased to a wide range of $22.00-28.00 from $30.00-32.00 on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was said to be trading near $15.00-17.00 per MWh.
December peak ECAR was talked higher at $20.25-20.50 from a range of $20.00-20.30 on Wednesday, while January/February ECAR was assessed steady near $21.80-22.25 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Friday were talked lower at $25.50-28.00 from $26.00-29.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.
December SPP was assessed higher at $22.10-22.25 from $21.75-22.05 on Wednesday, while January/February SPP was assessed steady at $22.95-23.15 per MWh, the sources said.
